# The Light That Arrives Unseen

## Scripture
"Before they call I will answer; while they are still speaking I will hear." — Isaiah 65:24

## Reflection
Tonight, if the sky is clear, look toward the constellation Perseus. During this season, its radiant point gives birth to one of autumn's most reliable celestial displays—the Perseid meteor showers, though their peak passed weeks ago. Yet here's the wonder: the meteors you might catch streaking across September's darkness were actually released by Comet Swift-Tuttle long ago, their debris now orbiting the sun in an ancient, faithful path.

Those brief flashes of light traveled millions of miles—some for centuries—before finally reaching your eyes in a single, sudden moment. The light arrives long after its source has moved on, unseen in its journey, yet undeniable in its arrival.

God's answers often work this way. Long before we form the words of our prayers, He has already set responses in motion. Like debris from a distant comet, His provision travels through unseen seasons—through circumstances, through the faithfulness of others, through quiet preparations in our own hearts—until the moment we need it most. The answer may feel sudden, but it was always coming.

We serve a God who speaks before we finish asking. Tonight, trust the unseen journeys of His grace.

## Prayer
Father, thank You for answering before we call. Help us trust that Your provision is already traveling toward us, even when we cannot yet see it. Give us patient hearts and watchful eyes. Amen.
